chmmc-cmm-2025-power-01a.title: Use a primitive root
chmmc-cmm-2025-power-01a.body:
Write $a\equiv g^k$. Squares of nonzero residues are $g^{2m}$, and $g^k\equiv g^{2m}$ forces $k\equiv2m\pmod{p-1}$; since $p-1$ is even this means $k$ is even. So $a$ is a quadratic residue iff $k$ is even.

Now $a^{(p-1)/2}\equiv g^{k(p-1)/2}$, which is $\equiv1$ iff $(p-1)\mid k\frac{p-1}2$ iff $k$ is even (because $g$ has order exactly $p-1$). Hence $a$ is a residue iff $a^{(p-1)/2}\equiv1$. ∎

chmmc-cmm-2025-power-01b.title: Euler's criterion
chmmc-cmm-2025-power-01b.body: Let $x=a^{(p-1)/2}$. Then $x^2=a^{p-1}\equiv1\pmod p$, so $(x-1)(x+1)\equiv0$ and $x\equiv\pm1$ because $p$ is prime. By part (a), $x\equiv1$ exactly when $a$ is a quadratic residue. Hence $x\equiv-1$ exactly when $a$ is a non-residue. ∎

chmmc-cmm-2025-power-02.title: CRT
chmmc-cmm-2025-power-02.body:
($\Rightarrow$) If $a\equiv x^2\pmod n$ with $\gcd(a,n)=1$, then reducing modulo $p_i^{e_i}$ gives $a\equiv x^2\pmod{p_i^{e_i}}$ and $\gcd(a,p_i)=1$.

($\Leftarrow$) Suppose $a\equiv x_i^2\pmod{p_i^{e_i}}$ with $p_i\nmid a$ for each $i$. By the Chinese Remainder Theorem pick $x$ with $x\equiv x_i\pmod{p_i^{e_i}}$ for all $i$. Then $x^2\equiv a$ modulo every $p_i^{e_i}$, hence modulo $n$, and $\gcd(a,n)=1$. ∎

chmmc-cmm-2025-power-03a.title: Count squares
chmmc-cmm-2025-power-03a.body: For nonzero $x,y$: $x^2\equiv y^2\iff p\mid(x-y)(x+y)\iff y\equiv\pm x$, and $x\not\equiv-x$ as $p$ is odd. So each nonzero square has exactly two square roots among the $p-1$ nonzero residues, giving $\frac{p-1}2$ distinct nonzero squares. ∎

chmmc-cmm-2025-power-03b.title: Euler's criterion
chmmc-cmm-2025-power-03b.body: By Euler's criterion (an integer $c\not\equiv0$ satisfies $c^{(p-1)/2}\equiv\left(\frac cp\right)\pmod p$, i.e. $\equiv\pm1$): $\left(\frac{ab}p\right)\equiv(ab)^{(p-1)/2}=a^{(p-1)/2}b^{(p-1)/2}\equiv\left(\frac ap\right)\left(\frac bp\right)\pmod p$. Both sides lie in $\{1,-1\}$ and $p>2$, so they are equal. ∎

chmmc-cmm-2025-power-03c.title: Factor by factor
chmmc-cmm-2025-power-03c.body: $\left(\frac{ab}n\right)=\prod_i\left(\frac{ab}{q_i}\right)=\prod_i\left(\frac a{q_i}\right)\left(\frac b{q_i}\right)=\left(\frac an\right)\left(\frac bn\right)$ by the multiplicativity of the Legendre symbol (which holds because $q_i\nmid a,b$). ∎

chmmc-cmm-2025-power-04a.title: Lift the square root
chmmc-cmm-2025-power-04a.body: Since $a\equiv x_1^2\pmod p$ with $p\nmid a$, $p\nmid x_1$. Suppose $a\equiv x_j^2\pmod{p^j}$ for some $j<k$. Try $x_{j+1}=x_j+tp^j$: $x_{j+1}^2\equiv x_j^2+2x_jtp^j\pmod{p^{j+1}}$. We need $2x_jt\equiv\frac{a-x_j^2}{p^j}\pmod p$, which is solvable for $t$ because $2x_j$ is invertible mod $p$. By induction $a\equiv x_k^2\pmod{p^k}$, and $\gcd(a,p)=1$. ∎

chmmc-cmm-2025-power-04b.title: Counting
chmmc-cmm-2025-power-04b.body:
Let $n=\prod p_i^{e_i}$. By the previous parts, a residue is a quadratic residue mod $n$ iff it is one modulo every $p_i^{e_i}$ (CRT), so the count is the product of the counts for each prime power.

Modulo $p^e$: a residue coprime to $p$ is a quadratic residue iff its reduction mod $p$ is a quadratic residue (previous problem). There are $\frac{p-1}2$ residue classes mod $p$ that are nonzero squares, and each has exactly $p^{e-1}$ lifts to residues mod $p^e$. So the count is $\frac{p-1}2p^{e-1}=\frac{\varphi(p^e)}2$.

Multiplying, the number of quadratic residues mod $n$ is $\prod\frac{\varphi(p_i^{e_i})}2=\frac{\varphi(n)}{2^m}$. ∎

chmmc-cmm-2025-power-05.title: Euler's criterion
chmmc-cmm-2025-power-05.body: By Euler's criterion $\left(\frac{-1}p\right)\equiv(-1)^{(p-1)/2}\pmod p$ and both sides are $\pm1$, so they are equal. $(p-1)/2$ is even iff $p\equiv1\pmod4$. ∎

chmmc-cmm-2025-power-06.title: Primes
chmmc-cmm-2025-power-06.body:
Let $p$ be an odd prime, $\zeta$ a primitive 8th root of unity in a field extension of $\mathbb F_p$ (it exists since $8\mid p^2-1$), and $\tau=\zeta+\zeta^{-1}$. Since $\zeta^4=-1$ we have $\zeta^2+\zeta^{-2}=0$, so $\tau^2=\zeta^2+2+\zeta^{-2}=2$, and $\tau\ne0$.

In characteristic $p$, $\tau^p=\zeta^p+\zeta^{-p}$. If $p\equiv\pm1\pmod8$, $\zeta^p=\zeta^{\pm1}$ and $\tau^p=\tau$. If $p\equiv\pm3\pmod8$, $\zeta^{\pm3}=-\zeta^{\mp1}$ (as $\zeta^4=-1$), so $\tau^p=-\tau$. On the other hand $\tau^p=\tau\,(\tau^2)^{(p-1)/2}=\tau\,2^{(p-1)/2}$. Cancelling $\tau$: $2^{(p-1)/2}\equiv1$ if $p\equiv\pm1\pmod 8$ and $\equiv-1$ if $p\equiv\pm3\pmod 8$. By Euler's criterion this is $\left(\frac2p\right)$.

chmmc-cmm-2025-power-06.title: Composite $n$
chmmc-cmm-2025-power-06.body: Let $f(n)=1$ for $n\equiv\pm1\pmod 8$ and $f(n)=-1$ for $n\equiv\pm3\pmod8$. Since $\{1,7\}$ is a subgroup of index $2$ in $(\mathbb Z/8)^\times$ and $f$ is the corresponding sign, $f(mn)=f(m)f(n)$. For $n=q_1\cdots q_m$ the Jacobi symbol is $\prod\left(\frac2{q_i}\right)=\prod f(q_i)=f(n)$. ∎

chmmc-cmm-2025-power-07a.title: Fermat
chmmc-cmm-2025-power-07a.body: By Fermat's little theorem $a^{p-1}\equiv1\pmod p$, so $\chi(a)^{p-1}=\chi(a^{p-1})=\chi(1)=1$ (using multiplicativity and periodicity; $\chi(1)=1$ because $\chi(1)^2=\chi(1)\ne0$). ∎

chmmc-cmm-2025-power-07b.title: Inverse
chmmc-cmm-2025-power-07b.body: $\chi(a)\chi(a^{-1})=\chi(aa^{-1})=\chi(1)=1$, so $\chi(a^{-1})=\chi(a)^{-1}$. By part (a) $\chi(a)$ is a root of unity, so $|\chi(a)|=1$ and $\chi(a)^{-1}=\overline{\chi(a)}$. ∎

chmmc-cmm-2025-power-07c.title: Shift trick
chmmc-cmm-2025-power-07c.body: If $\chi=\mathbf 1_p$ the sum is $p-1$. Otherwise choose $b$ with $\chi(b)\ne1$ (necessarily $p\nmid b$). As $t\mapsto bt$ permutes the residues, $S=\sum_t\chi(bt)=\chi(b)S$, so $(1-\chi(b))S=0$ and $S=0$. ∎

chmmc-cmm-2025-power-08a.title: Direct
chmmc-cmm-2025-power-08a.body: For $p\nmid a$, $\chi(a)^{p-1}=\chi(a^{p-1})=\chi(1)=1$ by Fermat's little theorem. ∎

chmmc-cmm-2025-power-08b.title: Powers of $g$
chmmc-cmm-2025-power-08b.body: Every residue $a\not\equiv0$ is $g^k$ for some $k$, so $\chi(a)=\chi(g)^k$; and $\chi(a)=0$ for $p\mid a$. Thus $\chi(g)$ determines $\chi$. ∎

chmmc-cmm-2025-power-08c.title: Bijection
chmmc-cmm-2025-power-08c.body: By the two previous parts, $\chi\mapsto\chi(g)$ is injective with values among the $(p-1)$-th roots of unity. Conversely for each $\omega$ with $\omega^{p-1}=1$ define $\chi_\omega(g^k)=\omega^k$ (well defined because $g^{k}\equiv g^{k'}$ iff $k\equiv k'\pmod{p-1}$ and $\omega^{p-1}=1$) and $\chi_\omega(a)=0$ for $p\mid a$; it is multiplicative and periodic. So there are exactly $p-1$ characters. ∎

chmmc-cmm-2025-power-09.title: Counting with a primitive root
chmmc-cmm-2025-power-09.body:
If $a\equiv0$ the only solution is $x=0$, and $\sum_{\chi\in E_n}\chi(0)=\mathbf 1_1(0)=1$ because every other $\chi\in E_n$ vanishes at $0$.

Let $a\not\equiv0$, $a=g^k$, and $d=\gcd(n,p-1)$. Solutions are $x=g^m$ with $nm\equiv k\pmod{p-1}$, which has $d$ solutions $m$ mod $p-1$ if $d\mid k$ and none otherwise.

The characters are $\chi_j(g)=\omega^j$ with $\omega=e^{2\pi i/(p-1)}$, $0\le j<p-1$, and $\chi_j^n=\mathbf 1_p$ iff $(p-1)\mid nj$ iff $j=t\frac{p-1}d$, $t=0,\dots,d-1$. Replacing $\chi_0=\mathbf1_p$ by $\mathbf 1_1$ does not change values at $a\not\equiv0$. So
$$\sum_{\chi\in E_n}\chi(a)=\sum_{t=0}^{d-1}\omega^{kt(p-1)/d}=\sum_{t=0}^{d-1}e^{2\pi ikt/d}=\begin{cases}d&d\mid k\\0&d\nmid k.\end{cases}$$
This matches the number of solutions. ∎

chmmc-cmm-2025-power-10a.title: Via a primitive root
chmmc-cmm-2025-power-10a.body: Let $\chi$ have order 2: $\chi(g)^2=1$ and $\chi(g)\ne1$ (else $\chi$ trivial by determination by $\chi(g)$), so $\chi(g)=-1$ and $\chi(g^k)=(-1)^k$. By Euler's criterion/previous work, $g^k$ is a quadratic residue iff $k$ is even, so $\chi(a)=\left(\frac ap\right)$ for all $a$. Conversely the Legendre symbol is multiplicative (shown earlier), periodic, and has order 2. ∎

chmmc-cmm-2025-power-10b.title: Orders
chmmc-cmm-2025-power-10b.body: Characters are $\chi_\omega$ with $\omega=\chi(g)$ a $(p-1)$-th root of unity, and the order of $\chi_\omega$ equals the multiplicative order of $\omega$, which divides $p-1$. Conversely for each $r\mid p-1$ the root of unity $e^{2\pi i/r}$ has order $r$. So order $r$ exists iff $r\mid p-1$, i.e. $p\equiv1\pmod r$. ∎

chmmc-cmm-2025-power-10c.title: Count
chmmc-cmm-2025-power-10c.body: Order dividing $n$ means $\chi(g)^n=1$, i.e. $\chi(g)$ is one of the $n$ $n$-th roots of unity, and each of them gives a character. Let $\chi_1(g)=e^{2\pi i/n}$. Then $\chi_1^j(g)=e^{2\pi ij/n}$, $j=0,\dots,n-1$, exhausts all $n$ choices, so every such character is a power of $\chi_1$. ∎

chmmc-cmm-2025-power-11.title: Substitution
chmmc-cmm-2025-power-11.body: As $t$ runs over the residues mod $p$ so does $s=at$, and $t=a^{-1}s$. Hence $g_a(\chi)=\sum_t\chi(t)\zeta^{at}=\sum_s\chi(a^{-1}s)\zeta^{s}=\chi(a^{-1})\sum_s\chi(s)\zeta^s=\chi(a^{-1})g_1(\chi)$. ∎

chmmc-cmm-2025-power-12c.title: Change of variable
chmmc-cmm-2025-power-12c.body:
Terms with $t=0$ or $t=1$ vanish, so $J(\chi, ar\chi)=\sum_{t
e0,1}\chi(t) ar\chi(1-t)=\sum_{t
e0,1}\chi\!\left( rac t{1-t}ight)$. The map $t\mapsto u= rac t{1-t}$ is a bijection from $\mathbb F_p\setminus\{0,1\}$ onto $\mathbb F_p\setminus\{0,-1\}$ (the value $-1$ would need $t=t-1$). Therefore $J=\sum_{u
e0,-1}\chi(u)=\sum_u\chi(u)-\chi(0)-\chi(-1)=0-0-\chi(-1)$. ∎

chmmc-cmm-2025-power-13.title: Direct
chmmc-cmm-2025-power-13.body: $\overline{J(\chi_1,\chi_2)}=\sum_t\overline{\chi_1(t)}\,\overline{\chi_2(1-t)}=J(\bar\chi_1,\bar\chi_2)$, where $\bar\chi_i$ are characters of modulus $p$ as well. ∎

chmmc-cmm-2025-power-14a.title: Evaluate the sixteen terms
chmmc-cmm-2025-power-14a.body:
Let $\psi=\chi^2$ (the Legendre symbol, since it has order 2). The set $E_4=\{\mathbf1_1,\chi,\psi,\bar\chi\}$. We use: $J(\mathbf1_1,\mathbf1_1)=p$; $J(\mathbf1_1,\phi)=J(\phi,\mathbf1_1)=0$ for $\phi\ne\mathbf1_p$ (character sum); $J(\phi_1,\phi_2)=J(\phi_2,\phi_1)$ (substitute $t\to1-t$); $J(\phi,\bar\phi)=-\phi(-1)$; $\overline{J(\phi_1,\phi_2)}=J(\bar\phi_1,\bar\phi_2)$.

Summing over the 16 pairs: $(\mathbf1_1,\mathbf1_1)\to p$; the 6 pairs with exactly one $\mathbf 1_1$ give $0$; $(\chi,\chi)$ and $(\bar\chi,\bar\chi)$ give $J(\chi,\chi)+\overline{J(\chi,\chi)}$; $(\chi,\psi),(\psi,\chi)$ give $2J(\chi,\psi)$ and $(\bar\chi,\psi),(\psi,\bar\chi)$ give $2\overline{J(\chi,\psi)}$ (as $\bar\psi=\psi$); $(\chi,\bar\chi),(\bar\chi,\chi)$ give $-2\chi(-1)$; $(\psi,\psi)$ gives $-\psi(-1)=-1$ (as $\psi(-1)=\chi(-1)^2=1$). Hence
$$\#(x^4+y^4\equiv1)=p+J(\chi,\chi)+\overline{J(\chi,\chi)}+2J(\chi,\chi^2)+2\overline{J(\chi,\chi^2)}-2\chi(-1)-1.$$

chmmc-cmm-2025-power-14a.title: The value of $\chi(-1)$
chmmc-cmm-2025-power-14a.body: Write $-1\equiv g^{(p-1)/2}$ with $g$ a primitive root and $\chi(g)=\pm i$. Then $\chi(-1)=(\pm i)^{(p-1)/2}$, which is $1$ iff $4\mid\frac{p-1}2$. And $-1=g^{(p-1)/2}$ is a fourth power iff $\gcd(4,p-1)=4$ divides $\frac{p-1}2$. So $-1$ is a fourth power iff $\chi(-1)=1$, and then the constant term is $-2-1=-3$. ∎

chmmc-cmm-2025-power-14b.title: Sum
chmmc-cmm-2025-power-14b.body: As in part (a), $\#(x^4+y^4\equiv1)=p+J(\chi,\chi)+\overline{J(\chi,\chi)}+2J(\chi,\chi^2)+2\overline{J(\chi,\chi^2)}-2\chi(-1)-1$ (terms: $J(\phi,\bar\phi)=-\phi(-1)$ for $\phi=\chi$ twice, $J(\psi,\psi)=-\psi(-1)=-1$ for the Legendre symbol $\psi=\chi^2$). Since $-1$ is not a fourth power, $\chi(-1)\ne1$, so $\chi(-1)=-1$ (it is $\pm1$), and the constant is $+2-1=+1$. ∎

chmmc-cmm-2025-power-15.title: Expand
chmmc-cmm-2025-power-15.body:
$g_a(\chi_1)g_a(\chi_2)=\sum_{s,t}\chi_1(s)\chi_2(t)\zeta^{a(s+t)}=\sum_u\zeta^{au}S(u)$ with $S(u)=\sum_{s+t=u}\chi_1(s)\chi_2(t)$.

For $u\ne0$ write $s=us',t=ut'$: $S(u)=\chi_1\chi_2(u)\sum_{s'+t'=1}\chi_1(s')\chi_2(t')=\chi_1\chi_2(u)J(\chi_1,\chi_2)$. For $u=0$: $S(0)=\sum_s\chi_1(s)\chi_2(-s)=\chi_2(-1)\sum_s\chi_1\chi_2(s)$.

(i) If $\chi_1\chi_2\ne\mathbf1_p$ then $S(0)=0$ and the product is $J\sum_{u\ne0}\chi_1\chi_2(u)\zeta^{au}=J\,g_a(\chi_1\chi_2)$.

(ii) Take $\chi_1=\chi$, $\chi_2=\bar\chi$ (so $\chi_1\chi_2=\mathbf1_p$): $S(0)=\bar\chi(-1)(p-1)=\chi(-1)(p-1)$ and for $u\ne0$, $S(u)=J(\chi,\bar\chi)=-\chi(-1)$. Since $\sum_{u\ne0}\zeta^{au}=-1$,
$$g_a(\chi)g_a(\bar\chi)=\chi(-1)(p-1)+\chi(-1)=\chi(-1)p.\ ∎$$

chmmc-cmm-2025-power-17.title: Absolute values
chmmc-cmm-2025-power-17.body: Taking absolute values in (i): $\sqrt p\cdot\sqrt p=|J|\cdot\sqrt p$ because $\chi_1,\chi_2,\chi_1\chi_2\ne\mathbf1_p$ all have Gauss sums of modulus $\sqrt p$. Hence $|J(\chi_1,\chi_2)|=\sqrt p$. ∎

chmmc-cmm-2025-power-18.title: Counting formula
chmmc-cmm-2025-power-18.body: By the counting formula, $\#(x^3+y^2\equiv1)=\sum_{\phi\in E_3,\ \phi'\in E_2}J(\phi,\phi')$ with $E_3=\{\mathbf1_1,\chi_2,\bar\chi_2\}$ and $E_2=\{\mathbf1_1,\chi_1\}$ (because $\chi_2^3=\mathbf1_p$ and $\chi_1^2=\mathbf1_p$). The pair $(\mathbf1_1,\mathbf 1_1)$ gives $p$; every pair with exactly one $\mathbf1_1$ gives $0$; the remaining pairs are $(\chi_2,\chi_1)$ and $(\bar\chi_2,\chi_1)$, giving $J(\chi_2,\chi_1)=J(\chi_1,\chi_2)$ and $J(\bar\chi_2,\chi_1)=J(\bar\chi_2,\bar\chi_1)=\overline{J(\chi_1,\chi_2)}$ (the quadratic character is real). ∎

chmmc-cmm-2025-power-19.title: Count with the Legendre symbol
chmmc-cmm-2025-power-19.body:
Let $\psi=\left(\frac\cdot p\right)$. For every residue $c$, $\#(x^2\equiv c)=1+\psi(c)$. So
$$N=\sum_{u+v\equiv5}(1+\psi(u))(1+\psi(v/2))=p+\sum_u\psi(u)+\sum_v\psi(v/2)+\sum_{u+v=5}\psi(u)\psi(v/2).$$
The two single sums vanish. Using $\psi(v/2)=\psi(2)\psi(v)$ and $u=5s$ (legitimate since $p\ne5$): $\sum_{u+v=5}\psi(u)\psi(v)=\psi(25)\sum_s\psi(s)\psi(1-s)=J(\psi,\psi)=-\psi(-1)$.

Therefore $N=p-\psi(2)\psi(-1)=p-\psi(-2)$. By the earlier results $\psi(-1)=1$ iff $p\equiv1\pmod 4$ and $\psi(2)=1$ iff $p\equiv\pm1\pmod8$: $\psi(-2)=1$ for $p\equiv1,3\pmod 8$ and $-1$ for $p\equiv5,7$. ∎

chmmc-cmm-2025-power-20.title: A congruence in $\mathbb Z[i]$
chmmc-cmm-2025-power-20.body:
$J=J(\chi,\chi)=\sum_{t\ne0,1}\chi(t(1-t))\in\mathbb Z[i]$, each term a unit. The involution $t\mapsto1-t$ fixes only $t=\frac12$, whose term is $\chi(\frac14)=\chi(4)^{-1}=\psi(2)$ ($\psi=\chi^2$ is the Legendre symbol, $\chi(4)=\chi(2)^2=\psi(2)$, real). The other $\frac{p-3}2$ values of $t$ split into pairs with equal terms:
$$J=\psi(2)+2U,\qquad U=\sum_{\text{pairs}}(\text{unit}).$$
Every unit of $\mathbb Z[i]$ is $\equiv1\pmod{1+i}$, so $U\equiv\frac{p-3}2\pmod{1+i}$ and $2U\equiv p-3\pmod{2(1+i)}$. Thus $J\equiv\psi(2)+p-3\pmod{2+2i}$, and since $4\in(2+2i)$ this depends only on the integer $\psi(2)+p-3\bmod4$:
- $p\equiv1\pmod8$: $\psi(2)=1$, $J\equiv-1$;
- $p\equiv5\pmod8$: $\psi(2)=-1$, $J\equiv1$.

Write $\varepsilon=-1$ resp. $+1$. $J=a+bi\equiv\varepsilon\pmod{2+2i}$ means $a-\varepsilon+bi=(2+2i)(m+ni)=2(m-n)+2(m+n)i$, so $b$ is even and $\frac{a-\varepsilon}2\equiv\frac b2\pmod2$.

chmmc-cmm-2025-power-20.title: Finish with $a^2+b^2=p$
chmmc-cmm-2025-power-20.body: Since $|J|^2=p$: $a^2+b^2=p$ with $b$ even, $a$ odd. If $p\equiv1\pmod8$: $b^2\equiv0\pmod8$ so $4\mid b$, hence $\frac{a+1}2$ is even and $a\equiv3\pmod4$. If $p\equiv5\pmod8$: $b^2\equiv4\pmod8$ so $b\equiv2\pmod4$, $\frac b2$ odd, so $\frac{a-1}2$ is odd and $a\equiv3\pmod4$. ∎

chmmc-cmm-2025-power-22a.title: Counting
chmmc-cmm-2025-power-22a.body: All products equal $1$, so $J$ and $J_0$ count the $n$-tuples $(t_i)$ of residues with prescribed sum: choose $t_1,\dots,t_{n-1}$ freely and $t_n$ is determined. That is $p^{n-1}$. ∎

chmmc-cmm-2025-power-22b.title: Eliminate one variable
chmmc-cmm-2025-power-22b.body:
Pick $k$ with $\chi_k=\mathbf1_1$ and $j$ with $\chi_j
e\mathbf1_1$ (so $\chi_j$ is nontrivial of modulus $p$). For any values of the other $t_i$ there is exactly one $t_k$ giving the required sum, and $\chi_k(t_k)=1$. Hence the sum equals $\sum_{(t_i)_{i
e k}\ 	ext{free}}\prod_{i
e k}\chi_i(t_i)=\prod_{i
e k}\Big(\sum_{t}\chi_i(t)\Big)$, which contains the factor $\sum_t\chi_j(t)=0$. The same works for the sum $\equiv0$. ∎

chmmc-cmm-2025-power-22c.title: Scaling
chmmc-cmm-2025-power-22c.body:
Let $\Phi=\chi_1\cdots\chi_n$. For $\lambda
ot\equiv0$ the substitution $t_i	o\lambda t_i$ preserves the condition $\sum t_i\equiv0$ and multiplies the summand by $\Phi(\lambda)$; so $J_0=\Phi(\lambda)J_0$. Choosing $\lambda$ with $\Phi(\lambda)
e1$ gives $J_0=0$.

Similarly let $S(u)=\sum_{t_1+\dots+t_n=u}\prod\chi_i(t_i)$. Then $S(0)=J_0=0$ and for $u
e0$ (put $t_i=us_i$) $S(u)=\Phi(u)J$. Therefore
$$\prod_ig_a(\chi_i)=\sum_{t_1,\dots,t_n}\prod\chi_i(t_i)\zeta^{a\sum t_i}=\sum_u\zeta^{au}S(u)=J\sum_{u
e0}\Phi(u)\zeta^{au}=J\,g_a(\Phi).\ ∎$$

chmmc-cmm-2025-power-22d.title: Reduce one variable
chmmc-cmm-2025-power-22d.body:
Let $S'(s)=\sum_{t_1+\dots+t_{n-1}=s}\prod_{i<n}\chi_i(t_i)$ and $J'=J(\chi_1,\dots,\chi_{n-1})$, $\Phi'=\chi_1\cdots\chi_{n-1}= ar\chi_n$. As in the previous problem, $S'(s)=\Phi'(s)J'$ for $s
e0$, and $S'(0)=J_0(\chi_1,\dots,\chi_{n-1})=0$ (for $n-1=1$ it is $\chi_1(0)=0$; for $n-1\ge2$ because $\Phi'
e\mathbf1_p$). Then
$$J(\chi_1,\dots,\chi_n)=\sum_sS'(s)\chi_n(1-s)=J'\sum_{s
e0} ar\chi_n(s)\chi_n(1-s)=J'\sum_{s
e0,1}\chi_n\!\left( rac{1-s}sight).$$
The map $s\mapsto w= rac{1-s}s$ is a bijection from $\mathbb F_p\setminus\{0,1\}$ onto $\mathbb F_p\setminus\{0,-1\}$, so the last sum is $\sum_{w
e0,-1}\chi_n(w)=0-\chi_n(-1)$. Hence $J=-\chi_n(-1)J'$. ∎

chmmc-cmm-2025-power-22e.title: Both formulas
chmmc-cmm-2025-power-22e.body:
Keep $S'(s)= ar\chi_n(s)J'$ for $s
e0$, $S'(0)=0$ from the previous problem ($J'=J(\chi_1,\dots,\chi_{n-1})$). Then
$$J_0=\sum_{t_n}\chi_n(t_n)S'(-t_n)=J'\sum_{t
e0}\chi_n(t) ar\chi_n(-t)=J'\sum_{t
e0} ar\chi_n(-1)=\chi_n(-1)(p-1)J'.$$
For the Gauss sums, with $S(u)=\sum_{\sum t_i=u}\prod\chi_i(t_i)$ as before: $S(0)=J_0$ and for $u
e0$, $S(u)=\mathbf 1_p(u)J=J=-\chi_n(-1)J'$ (by the previous problem). Hence
$$\prod g_a(\chi_i)=\sum_u\zeta^{au}S(u)=J_0+J\sum_{u
e0}\zeta^{au}=\chi_n(-1)(p-1)J'+\chi_n(-1)J'=\chi_n(-1)\,p\,J'.\ ∎$$

chmmc-cmm-2025-power-23.title: Expand
chmmc-cmm-2025-power-23.body:
Let $\chi$ have order $4$, so $E_4=\{\mathbf1_1,\chi,\chi^2,\chi^3\}$. By the counting formula, for $r\not\equiv0$: $N(r)=\sum_{(\chi_1,\chi_2,\chi_3)\in E_4^3}\chi_1\chi_2\chi_3(r)J(\chi_1,\chi_2,\chi_3)$, and for $r\equiv0$: $N(0)=\sum J_0(\chi_1,\chi_2,\chi_3)$.

* $(\mathbf1_1,\mathbf1_1,\mathbf1_1)$ contributes $p^2$ in both cases.
* Triples with some but not all $\chi_i=\mathbf1_1$ contribute $0$.
* The remaining $27$ triples $(\chi^a,\chi^b,\chi^c)$, $a,b,c\in\{1,2,3\}$: the product is trivial iff $a+b+c\equiv0\pmod4$, i.e. $\{a,b,c\}$ is a permutation of $(1,1,2)$ or of $(3,3,2)$: $6$ triples. The other $21$ have nontrivial product.

chmmc-cmm-2025-power-23.title: Bounds
chmmc-cmm-2025-power-23.body:
For $r\not\equiv0$: a triple with nontrivial product contributes absolute value $|J|=p$ (times $|\chi_1\chi_2\chi_3(r)|=1$): total $\le21p$; the $6$ triples with trivial product have $|J|=p^{3/2-1}=\sqrt p$: total $\le6\sqrt p$. So $|N(r)-p^2|\le21p+6\sqrt p$.

For $r\equiv0$: nontrivial-product triples contribute $J_0=0$; the $6$ trivial-product triples contribute $|J_0|=(p-1)\sqrt p$ each. So $|N(0)-p^2|\le6(p-1)\sqrt p$. ∎

chmmc-cmm-2025-power-24.title: Expand
chmmc-cmm-2025-power-24.body:
$g_a(\psi)^2=\sum_{s,t}\psi(s)\psi(t)\zeta^{a(s+t)}$. Terms with $t=0$ vanish. For $t
e0$ put $s=tw$ ($w$ runs over all residues): $\psi(tw)\psi(t)=\psi(w)\psi(t)^2=\psi(w)$, so
$$g_a(\psi)^2=\sum_w\psi(w)\sum_{t
e0}\zeta^{at(w+1)}.$$
The inner sum is $p-1$ if $w\equiv-1$ and $-1$ otherwise (as $p
mid a$). Hence $g_a(\psi)^2=\psi(-1)(p-1)-\sum_{w
e-1}\psi(w)=\psi(-1)(p-1)+\psi(-1)=\psi(-1)p$, because $\sum_w\psi(w)=0$. ∎

chmmc-cmm-2025-power-26.title: Additive characters
chmmc-cmm-2025-power-26.body:
$N=\frac1p\sum_{s\bmod p}\sum_{x}\zeta^{s(\sum a_ix_i^2-1)}=p^{n-1}+\frac1p\sum_{s\ne0}\zeta^{-s}\prod_{i=1}^n\Big(\sum_x\zeta^{sa_ix^2}\Big)$.

For $c\not\equiv0$: $\sum_x\zeta^{cx^2}=\sum_a(1+\psi(a))\zeta^{ca}=g_c(\psi)=\psi(c)g$ (using $g_c(\psi)=\psi(c^{-1})g=\psi(c)g$). Let $A=a_1\cdots a_n$. Then $\prod_i\psi(sa_i)g=\psi(s)^n\psi(A)g^n$ and
$$N=p^{n-1}+\frac{\psi(A)g^n}{p}\sum_{s\ne0}\psi(s)^n\zeta^{-s}.$$
*$n$ even:* $\psi(s)^n=1$, $\sum_{s\ne0}\zeta^{-s}=-1$, and $g^n=(\psi(-1)p)^{n/2}$, so $N=p^{n-1}-\psi(A)\psi(-1)^{n/2}p^{n/2-1}=p^{n-1}-\left(\frac{(-1)^{n/2}A}p\right)p^{(n-2)/2}$.

*$n$ odd:* $\sum_{s\ne0}\psi(s)\zeta^{-s}=g_{-1}(\psi)=\psi(-1)g$, hence $N=p^{n-1}+\frac{\psi(A)\psi(-1)g^{n+1}}p=p^{n-1}+\psi(A)\psi(-1)\,\psi(-1)^{(n+1)/2}p^{(n-1)/2}$, and $\psi(-1)^{1+(n+1)/2}=\psi(-1)^{(n-1)/2}$ (they differ by $\psi(-1)^2=1$), giving $N=p^{n-1}+\left(\frac{(-1)^{(n-1)/2}A}p\right)p^{(n-1)/2}$. ∎

chmmc-cmm-2025-power-27.title: Express $G_4$ by Gauss sums
chmmc-cmm-2025-power-27.body:
Let $\chi$ have order $4$, $\chi^2=\psi$. $G_4=\sum_t\#(n^4\equiv t)\zeta^t=\sum_t\sum_{\phi\in E_4}\phi(t)\zeta^t=\sum_{\phi}g(\phi)$ with $\phi\in\{\mathbf1_1,\chi,\psi,\bar\chi\}$; the term $\mathbf1_1$ gives $\sum_t\zeta^t=0$. So $G_4=g(\chi)+g(\psi)+g(\bar\chi)$ and, as $g(\psi)=G_2$,
$$G_4-G_2=g(\chi)+g(\bar\chi)=g(\chi)+\chi(-1)\overline{g(\chi)}.$$

chmmc-cmm-2025-power-27.title: Square
chmmc-cmm-2025-power-27.body:
$(G_4-G_2)^2=g(\chi)^2+\overline{g(\chi)}^2+2\chi(-1)|g(\chi)|^2$ (since $\chi(-1)^2=1$). By $g(\chi)^2=J(\chi,\chi)G_2$ and $G_2$ real, the first two terms sum to $G_2\cdot2a'$ where $J(\chi,\chi)=a'+b'i$; the last term is $2\chi(-1)p$. Hence
$$(G_4-G_2)^2=2a'G_2+2\chi(-1)p.$$
If $p\equiv1\pmod8$: $\left(\frac2p\right)=\chi(-1)=1$, and $a\equiv-1\equiv3\pmod 4$, so $a=a'$ (both satisfy $a^2+b^2=p$, $\equiv3\pmod4$, and $a'^2+b'^2=p$ with $a'\equiv3$ determine the sign of the odd member of the representation): $2(p+aG_2)$ as claimed.
If $p\equiv5\pmod8$: $\left(\frac2p\right)=-1$, $\chi(-1)=-1$ (by Problem 2.14's setting: $\chi(-1)=-1$ iff $-1$ is not a fourth power), $a\equiv1\pmod4$ so $a=-a'$ and $(G_4-G_2)^2=-2a G_2-2p=2\left(\frac2p\right)(p+aG_2)$. ∎

chmmc-cmm-2025-power-28.title: Fourier expansion of $\psi$
chmmc-cmm-2025-power-28.body:
Since $g_m(\psi)=\psi(m)g$ (also for $p\mid m$, both sides $0$) we have $\psi(m)=\frac1g\sum_{k=1}^{p-1}\psi(k)\zeta^{mk}$ with $g=G_2=i\sqrt p$. Therefore
$$L:=\sum_{m\text{ odd}}\frac{\psi(m)}m=\frac1g\sum_{k=1}^{p-1}\psi(k)\sum_{m\text{ odd}}\frac{\zeta^{mk}}m,$$
each inner series converging (Dirichlet test). As $p\equiv3\pmod4$, $\psi(p-k)=-\psi(k)$ and $\zeta^{m(p-k)}=\overline{\zeta^{mk}}$, so pairing $k$ with $p-k$:
$$L=\frac1g\sum_{k=1}^{(p-1)/2}\psi(k)\cdot2i\sum_{m\text{ odd}}\frac{\sin(m\theta_k)}m,\qquad\theta_k=\frac{2\pi k}p\in(0,\pi).$$

chmmc-cmm-2025-power-28.title: The sine series
chmmc-cmm-2025-power-28.body:
For $|z|<1$, $\sum_{m\text{ odd}}\frac{z^m}m=\frac12\ln\frac{1+z}{1-z}$; by Abel's theorem this extends to $z=e^{i\theta}$, $0<\theta<\pi$, where $\frac{1+z}{1-z}=i\cot\frac\theta2$ has argument $\frac\pi2$. Taking imaginary parts, $\sum_{m\text{ odd}}\frac{\sin m\theta}m=\frac\pi4$ for $0<\theta<\pi$.

Hence $L=\frac{1}{i\sqrt p}\cdot2i\cdot\frac\pi4\sum_{k=1}^{(p-1)/2}\psi(k)=\frac{\pi}{2\sqrt p}\sum_{k<p/2}\psi(k)$. Because $\psi(p-k)=-\psi(k)$, $\sum_{k>p/2}\psi(k)=-\sum_{k<p/2}\psi(k)$, so $\sum_{k<p/2}\psi(k)-\sum_{k>p/2}\psi(k)=2\sum_{k<p/2}\psi(k)$ and $L=\frac\pi{4\sqrt p}\big(\sum_{k<p/2}\psi(k)-\sum_{k>p/2}\psi(k)\big)$. ∎

chmmc-cmm-2025-power-29.title: Complete the square
chmmc-cmm-2025-power-29.body:
$J(\chi,\chi)=\sum_t\chi(t(1-t))$ and $t(1-t)=\frac14\big(1-(1-2t)^2\big)$. With $s=1-2t$ (a bijection of residues): $J(\chi,\chi)=\chi(4)^{-1}\sum_s\chi(1-s^2)$. Since $\#(s^2=v)=1+\psi(v)$,
$$\sum_s\chi(1-s^2)=\sum_v(1+\psi(v))\chi(1-v)=\sum_v\chi(1-v)+\sum_v\psi(v)\chi(1-v)=0+J(\psi,\chi),$$
as $\chi\ne\mathbf1_p$. Hence $K(\chi)=\chi(4)J(\chi,\chi)=J(\psi,\chi)=J(\chi,\psi)$ (symmetry $t\to1-t$). ∎

chmmc-cmm-2025-power-30.title: An identity for Jacobi sums
chmmc-cmm-2025-power-30.body:
**Identity.** For characters $\alpha,\beta$ with $\alpha,\beta,\alpha\beta\ne\mathbf1_p$: $J(\alpha,\beta)=\alpha(-1)J(\alpha,\overline{\alpha\beta})$. Indeed for $t\ne0,1$ put $u=\frac t{t-1}$ (a bijection of $\mathbb F_p\setminus\{0,1\}$); then $t=\frac u{u-1}$, $1-t=\frac1{1-u}$, so
$\alpha(t)\beta(1-t)=\alpha(u)\bar\alpha(u-1)\bar\beta(1-u)=\alpha(-1)\alpha(u)\,\overline{\alpha\beta}(1-u)$. Summing over $u$ gives the identity (the terms at $t,u\in\{0,1\}$ vanish since the characters are nontrivial).

chmmc-cmm-2025-power-30.title: Apply it
chmmc-cmm-2025-power-30.body:
$\chi$ has order $2k$, so $\psi=\chi^k$ is the quadratic character. By symmetry and the identity with $\alpha=\psi$, $\beta=\chi$ ($\alpha\beta=\chi^{k+1}\ne\mathbf1_p$ because $2\le k+1<2k$ for $k\ge2$, so $2k\nmid k+1$):
$$K(\chi)=J(\psi,\chi)=\psi(-1)J(\psi,\overline{\psi\chi})=\psi(-1)J(\psi,\chi^{-k-1})=\psi(-1)J(\psi,\chi^{k-1})=\psi(-1)K(\chi^{k-1}),$$
using $\chi^{-k-1}=\chi^{k-1}\chi^{-2k}=\chi^{k-1}$. (For $k=1$ the right side would involve the trivial character, so $k\ge2$ is needed.) ∎

chmmc-cmm-2025-power-31.title: Split $K$ and relate it to $\bar K$
chmmc-cmm-2025-power-31.body:
$K=\sum_t\chi(t)\psi(1-t)=A+B$, where $A=\sum_{t\text{ QR}}\chi(t)\psi(1-t)$ and $B=\sum_{t\text{ QNR}}\chi(t)\psi(1-t)$ (QR/QNR = quadratic residues/non-residues; $t=0$ gives $0$). Also $K(\chi^6)=J(\chi\psi,\psi)=\sum\chi(t)\psi(t)\psi(1-t)=A-B$.

By the identity $J(\alpha,\beta)=\alpha(-1)J(\alpha,\overline{\alpha\beta})$ (with $\alpha=\psi$, $\beta=\bar\chi$): $\bar K=J(\psi,\bar\chi)=\psi(-1)J(\psi,\psi\chi)=\psi(-1)\sum_t\psi(t)\psi(1-t)\chi(1-t)=\psi(-1)J(\psi\chi,\psi)=\psi(-1)(A-B)$.

If $p\equiv1\pmod4$ ($\psi(-1)=1$): $\bar K=A-B$, so $\operatorname{Re}K=\frac{K+\bar K}2=A$. If $p\equiv3\pmod4$: $\bar K=-(A-B)=B-A$, so $\operatorname{Re}K=B$.

chmmc-cmm-2025-power-31.title: Congruences modulo 2
chmmc-cmm-2025-power-31.body:
All values $\chi(t)$ are 10th roots of unity, so $A,B\in\mathbb Z[\zeta_{10}]=\mathbb Z[\zeta_5]$, and $\psi(1-t)=\pm1$ for $t\ne1$. Hence modulo $2\mathbb Z[\zeta_5]$ (note $\psi(1-t)\equiv1$):
$$A\equiv\sum_{t\text{ QR},\,t\ne1}\chi(t),\qquad B\equiv\sum_{t\text{ QNR}}\chi(t).$$
The quadratic residues form a group of order $\frac{p-1}2$ on which $\chi$ is a nontrivial character (it has order $5$ there), so $\sum_{t\text{ QR}}\chi(t)=0$ and the first sum is $-\chi(1)=-1$. The non-residues are $g\cdot$(residues), so $\sum_{\text{QNR}}\chi(t)=\chi(g)\sum_{\text{QR}}\chi=0$. Thus $A\equiv-1$ and $B\equiv0\pmod{2\mathbb Z[\zeta_5]}$.

Therefore if $p\equiv1\pmod 4$: $\operatorname{Re}K=A$ and $\frac{A+1}2\in\mathbb Z[\zeta_5]$ is an algebraic integer. If $p\equiv3\pmod 4$: $\operatorname{Re}K=B$ and $\frac B2\in\mathbb Z[\zeta_5]$ is an algebraic integer. ∎

chmmc-cmm-2025-power-32a.title: Real and imaginary elements of $\mathbb Z[\zeta_5]$
chmmc-cmm-2025-power-32a.body:
Let $\zeta=\zeta_5$; $\zeta,\zeta^2,\zeta^3,\zeta^4$ is a $\mathbb Z$-basis of $\mathbb Z[\zeta]$. Real elements are $m+n\frac{1+\sqrt5}2$ ($m,n\in\mathbb Z$). A purely imaginary element $Y$ satisfies $\bar Y=-Y$, which in the basis means $Y=\beta_1(\zeta-\zeta^{4})+\beta_2(\zeta^2-\zeta^3)$ with integers $\beta_j$. Numerically $\zeta-\zeta^{-1}=2i\sin72^\circ=i\sqrt{5+2\sqrt5}\,\frac{\sqrt5-1}2$ and $\zeta^2-\zeta^{-2}=2i\sin36^\circ=i\sqrt{5+2\sqrt5}\,\frac{3-\sqrt5}2$ (using $\sqrt{5-2\sqrt5}=(\sqrt5-2)\sqrt{5+2\sqrt5}$), so
$$Y=i\sqrt{5+2\sqrt5}\cdot\tfrac12\big[(3\beta_2-\beta_1)+(\beta_1-\beta_2)\sqrt5\big].\tag{$*$}$$
Moreover $c\sqrt{5+2\sqrt5}+d\sqrt{5-2\sqrt5}=\sqrt{5+2\sqrt5}\,\big[(c-2d)+d\sqrt5\big]$, so a number $\sqrt{5+2\sqrt5}\,(x+y\sqrt5)$ with $x,y\in\mathbb Z$ has this form with $d=y$, $c=x+2y$.

chmmc-cmm-2025-power-32a.title: Case $p\equiv1\pmod 4$
chmmc-cmm-2025-power-32a.body: $\operatorname{Re}K=A$ with $A+1\in2\mathbb Z[\zeta]$ real, so $A=-1+2(m+n\frac{1+\sqrt5}2)=(2m+n-1)+n\sqrt5$: integer coefficients. $i\operatorname{Im}K=B=2B'$ with $B'\in\mathbb Z[\zeta]$ imaginary; by $(*)$, $B=i\sqrt{5+2\sqrt5}\,[(3\beta_2-\beta_1)+(\beta_1-\beta_2)\sqrt5]$ with integers: of the required form.

chmmc-cmm-2025-power-32a.title: Case $p\equiv3\pmod 4$
chmmc-cmm-2025-power-32a.body: $\operatorname{Re}K=B=2B'$, $B'=m+n\frac{1+\sqrt5}2$, so $B=(2m+n)+n\sqrt5$. $i\operatorname{Im}K=A=Y$ is imaginary with $A+1\in2\mathbb Z[\zeta]$: $Y+1=(\beta_1-1)\zeta+(\beta_2-1)\zeta^2-(\beta_2+1)\zeta^3-(\beta_1+1)\zeta^4$ (using $1=-\zeta-\zeta^2-\zeta^3-\zeta^4$), so $\beta_1,\beta_2$ are odd, hence $3\beta_2-\beta_1$ and $\beta_1-\beta_2$ are even and $(*)$ gives $Y=i\sqrt{5+2\sqrt5}\,(x+y\sqrt5)$ with integers $x,y$. In both cases $K=a+b\sqrt5+ci\sqrt{5+2\sqrt5}+di\sqrt{5-2\sqrt5}$ with integers $a,b,c,d$. ∎

chmmc-cmm-2025-power-32b.title: The norm equation
chmmc-cmm-2025-power-32b.body:
Using $\sqrt{5+2\sqrt5}\sqrt{5-2\sqrt5}=\sqrt5$:
$$p=|K|^2=(a+b\sqrt5)^2+\big(c\sqrt{5+2\sqrt5}+d\sqrt{5-2\sqrt5}\big)^2=\big(a^2+5b^2+5c^2+5d^2\big)+\sqrt5\,\big(2ab+2c^2-2d^2+2cd\big).$$
Since $p$ is rational and $1,\sqrt5$ are linearly independent over $\mathbb Q$, the coefficient of $\sqrt5$ is $0$, i.e. $ab+cd=d^2-c^2$, and $a^2+5b^2+5c^2+5d^2=p$.

chmmc-cmm-2025-power-32b.title: The congruence mod 5
chmmc-cmm-2025-power-32b.body:
Let $\lambda=1-\zeta_5$, a prime of $\mathbb Z[\zeta_5]$ with residue field $\mathbb F_5$, $\lambda\mathbb Z[\zeta_5]\cap\mathbb Z=5\mathbb Z$. Take $\chi(g)=\zeta_{10}$; then $\chi(t)=\zeta_{10}^k$ for $t=g^k$ and $\zeta_{10}\equiv-1\pmod\lambda$ (since $\zeta_{10}=-\zeta_5^3$), so $\chi(t)\equiv(-1)^k=\psi(t)\pmod\lambda$. Hence
$$K=\sum_t\chi(t)\psi(1-t)\equiv\sum_t\psi(t)\psi(1-t)=J(\psi,\psi)=-\psi(-1)=(-1)^{(p+1)/2}\pmod\lambda.$$
On the other hand $\sqrt5=1+2(\zeta+\zeta^{-1})\equiv5\equiv0$, and $i\sqrt{5+2\sqrt5}=(\zeta-\zeta^{-1})\frac{1+\sqrt5}2\equiv0$, $i\sqrt{5-2\sqrt5}=(\sqrt5-2)\,i\sqrt{5+2\sqrt5}\equiv0\pmod\lambda$. So $K\equiv a\pmod\lambda$ and $a\equiv(-1)^{(p+1)/2}\pmod\lambda$; as $a$ is an integer this holds modulo $5$. ∎

chmmc-cmm-2025-power-33.title: Count $T$ modulo $p$ with power sums
Count $T$ exactly
chmmc-cmm-2025-power-33.body:
Solutions with $x=0$: $y^3=1$, $3$ solutions (as $3\mid p-1$); similarly $y=0$: $3$ solutions; $x=y=0$ is not a solution: $6$ in total. Solutions with $xy\ne0$: $a=x^3$, $b=y^3$ are nonzero cubes with $a+b=1$, and each such pair $(a,b)$ comes from $3\cdot3=9$ pairs $(x,y)$. Since $-1=(-1)^3$ is a cube, $a$ is a cube iff $-a$ is; so $a\mapsto-a$ is a bijection between the residues counted by $S$ ($a,a+1$ cubes, $a\ne0,-1$) and the nonzero cubes $c$ with $1-c$ a nonzero cube. Hence $T=6+9S$.

Combining: $6+9S\equiv-2-\binom{2k}k$, i.e. $\binom{2k}k\equiv-8-9S\pmod p$. ∎

chmmc-cmm-2025-power-34.title: Count
chmmc-cmm-2025-power-34.body:
If $x=0$: $y^3=1$ has $3$ solutions; if $y=0$: $3$ solutions; both zero is impossible. If $xy
e0$, then $a=x^3$ and $b=y^3=1-a$ are nonzero cubes, and each pair $(a,b)$ corresponds to $3\cdot3=9$ pairs $(x,y)$. As $-1$ is a cube, $c$ is a cube iff $-c$ is; so $a\mapsto-a$ maps $\{a
e0,1:a,1-a	ext{ cubes}\}$ bijectively onto $\{a'
e0,-1:a',a'+1	ext{ cubes}\}$, a set of size $S$. Hence $T=6+9S$. ∎

chmmc-cmm-2025-power-35.title: Nine terms
chmmc-cmm-2025-power-35.body: $J(\mathbf1_1,\mathbf1_1)=p$; the four pairs with exactly one $\mathbf1_1$ give $0$; $(\chi,\chi)$ and $(\bar\chi,\bar\chi)$ give $J+\bar J$ with $J=J(\chi,\chi)$; $(\chi,\bar\chi)$ and $(\bar\chi,\chi)$ give $-2\chi(-1)$, and $\chi(-1)=1$: indeed $\chi(-1)^2=\chi(1)=1$ so $\chi(-1)=\pm1$, and $\chi(-1)$ is a cube root of unity, hence $1$. So $T=p+J+\bar J-2$. ∎

chmmc-cmm-2025-power-36.title: Reduce to $S=0$
chmmc-cmm-2025-power-36.body: $\binom{2k}k+8\equiv-9S\pmod p$. Since $p\ne3$ and $0\le S\le p-2$, $p\mid\binom{2k}k+8\iff p\mid S\iff S=0$.

chmmc-cmm-2025-power-36.title: When is $S=0$?
chmmc-cmm-2025-power-36.body: $S=0$ means $T=6$, i.e. $p-2+2\operatorname{Re}J(\chi,\chi)=6$, so $p-8=-2\operatorname{Re}J\le2|J|=2\sqrt p$. Then $(\sqrt p-1)^2\le9$, $\sqrt p\le4$, $p\le16$. The primes $\equiv1\pmod3$ up to $16$ are $7$ and $13$. Check: modulo $7$ the nonzero cubes are $\{1,6\}$; $a=1$ gives $a+1=2$ (not a cube) and $a=6=-1$ is excluded, so $S=0$. Modulo $13$ the nonzero cubes are $\{1,5,8,12\}$; $a=1,5,8$ give $2,6,9$ (not cubes), $a=12=-1$ excluded, so $S=0$. (Indeed $\binom42+8=14$ and $\binom84+8=78=6\cdot13$.) Hence the primes are exactly $7$ and $13$. ∎

chmmc-cmm-2025-power-37.title: $J\in\mathbb Z[\omega]$
chmmc-cmm-2025-power-37.body: Take $\omega=\chi(g)$. Then $\chi$ takes values in $\{0,1,\omega,\omega^2\}$, so $J=J(\chi,\chi)\in\mathbb Z[\omega]$, $J=a+b\omega$ with $a,b\in\mathbb Z$.

chmmc-cmm-2025-power-37.title: Gauss sums mod 3
chmmc-cmm-2025-power-37.body:
$\chi(-1)=1$ (a cube root of unity that is $\pm1$). From $g(\chi)^2=J\,g(\bar\chi)$ and $g(\chi)g(\bar\chi)=p$ we get $g(\chi)^3=pJ$.

Let $\mathcal O$ be the ring of integers of $\mathbb Q(\omega,\zeta_p)$. For algebraic integers $u_i$, $(\sum u_i)^3\equiv\sum u_i^3\pmod{3\mathcal O}$ (since $(x+y)^3=x^3+y^3+3xy(x+y)$). Hence
$$g(\chi)^3\equiv\sum_{t\ne0}\chi(t)^3\zeta_p^{3t}=\sum_{t\ne0}\zeta_p^{3t}=-1\pmod{3\mathcal O}.$$
So $pJ\equiv-1\pmod{3\mathcal O}$. As $p\equiv1\pmod3$, $pJ+1=(p-1)J+(J+1)$ and $(p-1)J\in3\mathcal O$, thus $\frac{J+1}3\in\mathcal O\cap\mathbb Q(\omega)=\mathbb Z[\omega]$. So $J+1=3(m+n\omega)$, i.e. $a=3m-1\equiv2$ and $b=3n\equiv0\pmod3$. ∎

chmmc-cmm-2025-power-38b.title: Elements of norm $p$
chmmc-cmm-2025-power-38b.body:
In the Euclidean domain $\mathbb Z[\omega]$ (norm $N(m+n\omega)=m^2-mn+n^2$), $p\equiv1\pmod3$ splits as $p=\pi\bar\pi$ with $\pi=a+b\omega$ and $\bar\pi$ non-associate primes. An element of norm $p$ is a unit times $\pi$ or $\bar\pi$; the six units are $\pm1,\pm\omega,\pm\omega^2$.

The residue ring $\mathbb Z[\omega]/(3)$ has $9$ elements and $6$ units (elements not divisible by $1-\omega$). No unit $u\ne1$ is $\equiv1\pmod 3$ (the norms of $u-1$ are $4,3,3,1,1$, none divisible by $9$), so the six units have distinct residues mod $3$, and therefore they represent all six unit residues. Consequently for each of $\pi$, $\bar\pi$ (which are coprime to $3$), exactly one of its six associates is $\equiv-1\pmod3$, i.e. has the form $m+n\omega$ with $m\equiv2$, $n\equiv0\pmod3$.

chmmc-cmm-2025-power-38b.title: Conclusion
chmmc-cmm-2025-power-38b.body: So there are exactly two elements of norm $p$ of the form $m+n\omega$, $m\equiv2$, $n\equiv0\pmod 3$: $a+b\omega$ and its conjugate $a+b\bar\omega=(a-b)-b\omega$ (it also satisfies the congruences, and differs from $a+b\omega$ since $b\ne0$ as $p$ is not a square). Hence the only pairs are $(a,b)$ and $(a-b,-b)$. ∎

chmmc-cmm-2025-power-39.title: $2$ is a cube iff $b$ is even
$b$ even iff $p=x^2+27y^2$
chmmc-cmm-2025-power-39.body: If $b$ is even then $b=6y$ ($3\mid b$) and $4p=(2a-b)^2+3b^2$ gives $p=(a-3y)^2+27y^2$. Conversely suppose $p=x^2+27y^2$; as $p\equiv1\pmod 3$, $x\equiv\pm1$ and we may take $x\equiv2\pmod3$. The element $x+3y(1+2\omega)=(x+3y)+6y\omega$ has norm $x^2+27y^2=p$ and satisfies $x+3y\equiv2$, $6y\equiv0\pmod3$. By the uniqueness statement, $6y=\pm b$, so $b$ is even. ∎

chmmc-cmm-2025-power-40.title: Compute
chmmc-cmm-2025-power-40.body: $\binom{2k}k\equiv-T-2=-(p-2+J+\bar J)-2\equiv-(J+\bar J)\pmod p$, and $J+\bar J=2a+b(\omega+\bar\omega)=2a-b$. So $\binom{2k}k\equiv-2a+b\pmod p$. ∎

chmmc-cmm-2025-power-41.title: Bound $p$
chmmc-cmm-2025-power-41.body: Put $N=-2a+b$. Then $N\equiv-4+0\equiv2\pmod3$, and $r\not\equiv2$, so $N-r\ne0$. If $\binom{2k}k\equiv r\pmod p$ then $p\mid N-r$, so $p\le|N-r|\le|2a-b|+|r|$. From $4p=(2a-b)^2+3b^2$ we get $|2a-b|\le2\sqrt p$. So $p\le2\sqrt p+|r|$, which bounds $p$ (namely $\sqrt p\le1+\sqrt{1+|r|}$). Hence only finitely many such primes. ∎
